claims.text: Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
A page exists at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ documenting the Terraform/OpenTofu state backend (the 'state backend guide').
The self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service environment variable `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` specifies the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API.
When `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is unset on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes are not registered.
`PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` may be set to the same value as `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service, so a separate domain/DNS record for the Terraform-compatible API is not required.
The DNS record for the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` domain should point at the same host that serves `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` in a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud deployment.

The state backend guide uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain for the Pulumi Cloud Terraform-compatible state backend, in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.

For a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud Terraform state backend, the `TF_TOKEN_*` environment variable name, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration use the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` value as the hostname.
